source_message.text:
Hello—I received the email below from contracts, and I think some of the information may have been left incomplete.

Good Morning,

I hope you're doing well.

The necessary changes for each site's subcontractor agreement are listed below. After making the edits, please send us updated versions of every subcontractor agreement. We hope these details are helpful and make the process faster.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Could you make these revisions as well? Sorry, I have changes for these two budgets. For NCA, the allocated budget for NH is $18750; the start date was 9/8, and it ends on 10/20.

The site labeled 286R, which is actually 201, has a budget of $16200. They started on 9/3 and will also end on 10/22. She also said:

"The number of weeks served on Annex B Page 5 is incorrect. It is listed as 11.5 weeks, but the correct total is 7 weeks. Please update the number ASAP so we can ensure everything is accurate and the payments are correct."

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I can't complete the edits or finalize either document until you confirm the following details.

1\. Weeks correction (both NCA and 286R/201): On Annex B Page 5, changing the weeks column from 11.5 to 7 while leaving the hourly rates and hours unchanged would push both salary totals far below the current subcontract amounts. NCA would go from $12,650.00 to about $7,700 against an $18,750 total, while 286R/201 would fall from $10,925.00 to about $6,650 against a $16,200 total. Should I close those gaps by increasing the hourly rates or hours, or should I place the difference in a non-personnel line such as Consumable Supplies or Equipment, following the approach used for HPI and MS 284?

2\. 286R or 201: Please confirm which name belongs on the final document. The Contract ID # for this site is also blank; do you have it?

3\. NCA Contract ID #: This field is blank as well. Can you provide that number?

4\. 286R/201 Amount Allocated in the Budget field: Instead of a dollar amount, the field currently contains 65%. Should it show the site's full program allocation, as with HPI at $24,000 and MS 284 at $31,500?

5\. NCA dates: Two different ranges currently appear in the same document—the Term section shows 8/30/27 to 10/15/27, while the Schedule table shows 9/1/27 to 10/8/27. With the new dates set for 9/8 to 10/20, should both the Term line and Schedule table be updated to match, or does one of the existing ranges need to remain?

Once you answer these questions, I can finalize both documents.

ambiguity.description: The NCA agreement contains conflicting date ranges, and it is unresolved whether the supplied replacement dates should be applied to both the Term section and Schedule table.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: 1\. Follow the same approach used for HPI, but put the difference only in approved lines such as travel and consumable supplies. 2. Since she did not provide a contract ID, use 286R; it is confusing because the funding comes from one school while the program is hosted at another location. 3. The NCA contract ID is the same situation—it was not provided. 4. Use the numbers she supplied when I asked, although I don't think she knows the correct answer. 5. To keep everything consistent, apply the dates she gave us to all of the date fields. She has been especially difficult to work with and still hasn't supplied the information we need for our schedules, so hopefully the documents won't get kicked back again.
